title: State of NCT of Delhi v. Chandrakant Jha (The Butcher of Delhi)
crime_type: Serial Decapitation Homicide / Taunting Letters to Law Enforcement
court_or_authority: High Court of Delhi / Sessions Court Tis Hazari, Delhi
legal_citation: Criminal Appeal No. 41/2013; 2016 SCC OnLine Del 641; 2016 CriLJ 2185
source: High Court of Delhi Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1928172)
ipc_sections: Section 201 IPC (Causing disappearance of evidence of offence)
location: Hari Nagar, Alipur & Tihar Central Jail Gate, New Delhi, India
evidence: Recovery of decapitated, limbless human torsos wrapped in gunny sacks deposited outside Gate No. 3 of Tihar Central Jail
Handwritten taunting letters addressed to Delhi Police challenging detectives to identify perpetrator
Forensic handwriting identification confirming handwriting matches Chandrakant Jha's specimen handwriting
Seizure of heavy kitchen cleavers, butcher knives, and plastic ropes from rented room in Alipur, Delhi
Blood splatter DNA analysis on bathroom tiles and floor drain traps in suspect's rented residence matching victims
modus_operandi: Befriended young male migrant laborers seeking work at Azadpur agricultural wholesale market. Offered lodging and informal employment in his vegetable trade. Monitored victims for perceived moral infractions or insolence. Bound sleeping victims, strangled them with rope, decapitated and dismembered remains in the bathroom, boiled parts to prevent rapid putrefaction, packed torsos into baskets, and left them directly outside Tihar Jail with handwritten taunts to police.
personality_disorder: Forensic psychiatric profiling: Severe Antisocial Personality Disorder with Narcissistic and Sadistic traits, deep-seated institutional paranoia and vengeance against Delhi Police and prison authorities.
common_traits: Dropping remains in front of high-security correctional facilities (Tihar Jail)
Extreme retributive violence over minor perceived slights
summary: Infamous Delhi serial killings where the accused murdered and dismembered victims, dumping their remains outside Tihar Jail with handwritten notes challenging police. The Delhi High Court upheld his murder convictions, commuting death to life imprisonment without remission.
